cards.text: Israel's on the move again, friend. They camp in the plains of Moab near the Jordan, across from Jericho. And Balak son of Zippor has seen ALL that Israel did to the Amorites.

cards.question: Moab is terrified of the Israelites. What reason does the text give?

answers.text: There are so many of them

cards.text: So Moab tells the elders of Midian, "This horde will devour everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field." And Balak son of Zippor is king of Moab at that time.

cards.question: King Balak sends messengers to summon a man named Balaam son of Beor. Where does Balaam live?

cards.text: Balak's message: "Behold, a people has come out of Egypt," said Balak. "They cover the face of the land and have settled next to me." Friend, that's a man peeking through the blinds at his new neighbors ALL DAY.

cards.question: So what does King Balak want Balaam to come and do to this people?
Balak tells Balaam he knows that those Balaam blesses are blessed, and those he curses are cursed.

cards.text: So the elders of Moab and Midian head out with the fees for divination in hand. They did NOT come all that way for a free estimate.

cards.question: The elders tell Balaam everything King Balak said. What does Balaam tell them?

answers.text: Stay the night for the LORD's answer
Leave the payment and go home
Wait here while he packs his bags

cards.text: Then God comes to Balaam and asks, "Who are these men with you?" And Balaam tells God the whole message from Balak: come and curse this people for me.

cards.question: God tells Balaam, "Do not go with them." Then He says Balaam is not to curse this people. What reason does God give?
The next morning, Balaam tells Balak's princes that the LORD has refused to let him go with them.

cards.text: So Balak sends other princes, MORE of them, and more distinguished than the first. First batch didn't work? Send a bigger batch with FANCIER sprinkles.

cards.question: The new princes bring King Balak's message to Balaam. What does Balak promise him this time?

answers.text: To give him half of Moab

cards.question: Balaam says that even if Balak gave him his house full of silver and gold, he could not go beyond the ___ of the LORD his God.

cards.text: Then Balaam asks them to stay overnight like the others did, so he can find out what else the LORD has to tell him. Friend, this man's guest room stays BOOKED.

cards.question: That night God comes to Balaam again. What does God tell him this time?

answers.text: Go with them but do only what I say
Send these men home for good
Stay here and bless Moab instead

cards.text: So in the morning Balaam saddles his donkey and heads out with the princes of Moab. Road trip! What could POSSIBLY go wrong?

cards.question: Balaam is on the road with the princes of Moab. How does God respond to Balaam going along?

answers.text: He goes ahead to bless him

cards.text: And the angel of the LORD stands in the road to oppose him. Balaam's riding along on his donkey, his two servants with him, just cruising.

cards.question: Balaam's donkey sees the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. What does she do?

cards.text: So Balaam beats her to get her back on the path. Then the angel of the LORD stands in a narrow passage between two vineyards, with walls on either side.

cards.question: Walls on both sides, and the donkey sees the angel of the LORD again. What does she do?

cards.text: And she crushes Balaam's foot against the wall, so he beats her again. Then the angel moves on ahead to a narrow place with no room to turn right or left.

cards.question: No room to turn right or left, and the donkey sees the angel of the LORD one more time. What does she do?

cards.text: Balaam is FURIOUS, and he beats her with his staff. Friend, that donkey is having a worse week than I had in the back of the junk drawer, and I was UNDER THE TAKEOUT MENUS.

cards.question: Balaam has just beaten his donkey a third time. Then the LORD does something nobody expects. What is it?

answers.text: He sends a storm on the road

cards.text: And she says to Balaam, "What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?" Friend. The DONKEY. Is TALKING.

cards.question: And Balaam talks right back to his donkey like it's a regular Tuesday. What does he tell her?

answers.text: You have made a fool of me
Who taught you how to speak

cards.question: The donkey asks Balaam if she has ever treated him this way before, and Balaam says yes.

cards.text: Balaam told her that if he had a sword in his hand, he'd kill her right now. Then the LORD opens his eyes, and there's the angel of the LORD with a drawn sword in HIS hand.

cards.question: Balaam finally sees the angel of the LORD standing in the road. What does he do?

cards.text: The angel of the LORD asks him, "Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is perverse before me."

cards.question: The angel says the donkey saw him and turned away these three times. What does he say would have happened if she hadn't?

answers.text: He would have killed the donkey
He would have let Balaam pass

cards.question: So the donkey saved Balaam's life. What are Balaam's first words back to the angel of the LORD?
Balaam offers to go back home if this is displeasing to the angel. What does the angel of the LORD tell him?

answers.text: Go but speak only what I say

cards.text: So Balaam goes with the princes of Balak. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: Balak son of Zippor first appears here with no word on who he is. The reader only learns he is king of Moab two cards later, on card 3.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "What reason does the text give?" sounds like a test question, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: Balaam son of Beor is brought in only as "a man named Balaam." Nothing says who he is (Joshua 13:22 calls him the diviner), so the baker has no idea why a king would summon him.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Balaam tells God the whole message from Balak" isn't true to the text. Balaam's retelling in 22:11 leaves out Balak's line about those Balaam blesses and curses (22:6), and it changes "defeat them" to "fight against them."

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Numbers 22:14 is never told. The princes go back and report only that "Balaam refused to come with us," which drops the fact that it was the LORD who refused. That is an important detail, and it explains why Balak just sends more princes.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "Road trip! What could POSSIBLY go wrong?" signals that trouble is coming. That rules out "He is pleased with him" and "He goes ahead to bless him" on card 2, which asks how God responds to Balaam going along.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Both the question and card 7 say there is no room to turn right or left. That rules out the wrong answer "Turns around and runs."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke compares the donkey's situation to the drawer. The donkey's core action is being beaten again and again for trying to help, but the drawer was about being forgotten in the dark, so the two don't share an action. Ranking the donkey's beating against his drawer years doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup line "talks right back to his donkey like it's a regular Tuesday" says Balaam isn't surprised. That rules out the wrong answer "Who taught you how to speak," and it makes "Forgive me for hitting you" unlikely too.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This card comes after card 13 (22:30) but goes back to tell Balaam's sword threat from 22:29 ("Balaam told her..."). It steps backward through the passage instead of moving forward. The threat belongs with or before card 13.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
